intro: Pick the situation closest to yours. Each one is a short route through the site: what to learn first, what to watch, the decision to make, the build to follow, the number to check, and a worked example. The brief builder below turns your answers into a checklist you can take into a design review.

situations.title: Add an assistant to a product you already run
situations.when: Users ask questions, the assistant answers from your docs or data, and a person still presses the buttons.

steps.label: What a language model does
steps.why: Context, tokens and hallucination are the three things that will bite first.

steps.label: Retrieval (RAG)
steps.why: Your facts come from retrieval, not from the model.

steps.label: The policy specialist retrieves, with provenance
steps.why: Every answer cites the passage it came from.

steps.label: Gate 04: where does every fact come from?
steps.why: Grounding is the gate an assistant lives or dies by.

steps.label: Playbook: Data & AI platform
steps.why: Governed data is what makes retrieval trustworthy.

steps.label: Availability and recovery budget
steps.why: An assistant that is down is a support ticket, not a feature.

steps.label: The damaged-order case, one-agent design
steps.why: Policy on the desk, cited, before a reply is drafted.

situations.title: Let an agent act on customer records
situations.when: Refunds, tickets, orders, accounts. The agent proposes and sometimes executes writes that cost money or trust.

steps.label: Running it safely
steps.why: Identity, checks in code, approval and the kill switch.

steps.label: A refund denied before execution
steps.why: The gate decides, whatever the model said.

steps.label: A planted instruction blocked by a check
steps.why: Assume injected text will be followed; design so it cannot do harm.

steps.label: Gate 05: is every write typed, validated, idempotent and reversible?
steps.why: The write path is the whole risk.

steps.label: Playbook: Agentic AI
steps.why: The questions first, then the build in order.

steps.label: Availability and recovery budget
steps.why: Decide the recovery time before the first incident.

steps.label: The damaged-order case: $84 refund, over the $50 approval line
steps.why: Allowed for this identity, routed to a person, verified against records.

situations.title: Automate a back-office process end to end
situations.when: A multi-step process with handoffs, documents and systems of record, where today a person carries the context.

steps.label: Four questions decide whether an agent is the right call
steps.why: Most of these processes want a workflow with a model inside, not an agent.

steps.label: What makes it an agent
steps.why: Know the loop before you buy one.

steps.label: Coordinator and specialist: a bounded work order
steps.why: What a specialist is given, and what it is not.

steps.label: Gate 07: what does a run cost at ten times the volume?
steps.why: Back-office volumes make per-run cost the architecture.

steps.label: Playbook: Application modernization
steps.why: The process usually lives in a system that needs an API first.

steps.label: Availability and recovery budget
steps.why: What the process can tolerate when the agent is down.

steps.label: Budget exhausted: a bounded exit
steps.why: A run that stops on its limit and hands off is the design working.

situations.title: Put a knowledge system on company documents
situations.when: Search and answers over policies, contracts, manuals. The hard part is who may see what, and proving where an answer came from.

steps.label: Embeddings
steps.why: How 'similar' is computed, and why two models' vectors do not mix.

steps.label: Retrieval (RAG)
steps.why: Owned, versioned, permission-filtered sources.

steps.label: Retrieval with provenance, in the flagship lesson
steps.why: The passage, its owner and its review date arrive together.

steps.label: Gate 03: what may the agent see, per user, enforced by the platform?
steps.why: A document index that ignores permissions is a breach waiting to happen.

steps.label: Playbook: Data & AI platform
steps.why: Someone owns each layer.

steps.label: Gate check
steps.why: Score the design before the first index is built.

steps.label: No covering policy found: the run asks a person
steps.why: What a knowledge system should do when it has no evidence.

situations.title: Coordinate several agents
situations.when: A coordinator that delegates to specialists. The question is what each one owns and how much the coordination costs.

steps.label: Multi-agent systems
steps.why: Hub and spoke, and why a mesh does not scale.

steps.label: Coordinator and policy specialist
steps.why: A work order out, a structured result back, and a specialist that cannot refund.

steps.label: Gate 02: what does each agent own, where does control pass, where does a human sit?
steps.why: Ownership is the design.

steps.label: Coordination cost: n(n-1)/2 against n-1
steps.why: Count the links before you count the agents.

steps.label: Playbook: Agentic AI
steps.why: Multi-agent workflows in Azure AI Foundry over governed data.

steps.label: The specialist's permissions are configuration, not nature
steps.why: A separate context is not a separate permission set.

situations.title: Decide whether AI belongs here at all
situations.when: Leadership is asking what you have, where AI would pay off first, and what has to be true before you let it act.

steps.label: Should we build one?
steps.why: The questions, the ladder and the gates, in order.

steps.label: The estate map: where AI can go
steps.why: Six layers you already have, seven places AI can go.

steps.label: The autonomy ladder
steps.why: Pick the rung the estate underneath can support.

steps.label: Run the gate check
steps.why: A score and a record you can take into the room.

steps.label: The six playbooks
steps.why: What a principal architect is asked to own, each with the questions first.

steps.label: One request, every gate it crosses
steps.why: Fifteen steps that show where each decision sits.

brief.intro: Answer four questions. The brief lists the gates, lessons and checks that apply to your system. Nothing leaves your browser.

questions.q: Will it execute actions that change records, money or messages?
Will it see data about identifiable people or tenants?
questions.no: No, public or internal reference data only

questions.q: Will it read content it does not control (email, web pages, uploads, tickets)?
Will more than one agent be involved?
